insight: SSIM vs goldens lands at ~0.998 across runs (cursor position noise is negligible); run-to-run t_agent spread was 9278-9334 on runs 2-3 with run 1 warmer at 11554 — median of 3 absorbs the cold-start outlier.

idea: idea 1: warm verb (pre-boot daemon+recorder, start attaches)
insight: The frozen bench calls `start` directly and would never exercise a separate `warm` command, so the perceived-zero start can never show up in T_agent under this harness. Any warm-path win must instead come from making `start` itself cheaper (ideas 2/3) or from a harness change (needs human sign-off, like idea 16).

idea: idea 3: start-path poll tightening (ping 150→50ms, waitForFile 200→50ms, connectCdp 300→100ms, recorder post-goto 300ms sleep removed)
insight: 606ms (6.5%) came purely from poll granularity and a dead insurance sleep — no behavior change, SSIM unchanged (~0.998). Run 1 was 10750ms (cold after daemon-code change) and median-of-3 absorbed it again; the post-goto 300ms sleep in recorder.mjs was pure latency since the ready-file is only written after it, and G1/G2/G6 confirm listeners attach fine without it. Remaining start cost is dominated by Chromium boot itself, so idea 2 (persistent browser) is the next lever on this phase.

idea: idea 4: floor-find DOM-quiet window (120ms) and STEP_GAP_MS (200ms)
gates: G3-class fail on every probe (submit races date commit)
insight: The floor is essentially where we already are. Probes 30/50, 60/100, 60/150 (last two at true idle) all failed identically: the OK click lands while the rc-picker popup from the end-date fill is still open/uncommitted — record never created, education-list stays empty. Green boundary sits between pace 108ms (fail) and 161ms (baseline pass) before the submit click, so STEP_GAP_MS 200 is already ~1.25x the floor and quiet=120 has at most ~420ms (4.8%) recoverable — under the 5% bar even in the best case. The gap is not dead time; it is masking the DatePicker async commit. NEW IDEA seeded: replace the fixed gap with a commit-verified wait after picker fills (wait for .ant-picker-dropdown to close / value to commit), which would let the gap drop to ~50ms safely and also de-risk idea 6.

idea: idea 8: signal-based recorder stop (spec-flush wait + SIGTERM, no stop-file poll / 900ms flush sleep)
insight: The mechanism works: finish phase dropped 3036→1738/1874/1741ms (-1.2s, consistent) with all gates green on all 4 runs — the 900ms flush sleep and 250ms polls are pure latency, and a green live assert already guarantees the final click was captured (ContextClosed flushes it). But the scoring median was 8615 (-1.3%, under the 5% bar) because run-to-run noise was 27% (cold start 3371ms, one plan phase +1.1s) vs the ~3% the protocol assumes — machine was never truly idle (conductor workspaces + VM). Cleanest run hit 7645ms. Diff saved to results/sigterm-stop.patch; re-apply and re-score 3 runs on a genuinely idle machine — expected median ~7600-7700, a clear KEEP. Stopped mid-experiment by user request before the strictly-gated re-score could run.
